newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: First Kekwah crude exports in August - Petronas.
newsitem.headline: First Kekwah crude exports in August - Petronas.

text.p: Malaysia's state-owned Petronas plans to make the first exports of its new Bunga Kekwah crude blend in August, a spokesman said on Wednesday.
Market sources had earlier expected first exports in July.
Petronas trading arm Petco is working on the first sale of the crude.
The crude is expected to compete with Indonesia's benchmark Minas crude, although it will be priced off Tapis.
The crude has an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 36.5 degrees and sulphur content of just 0.05 percent.
The gas oil and low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) yields are 40 percent each.
The spokesman said production will start in July at 20,000 barrels per day (bpd), building to 40,000 bpd by 2000.
The crude will be loaded from a 60,000-dwt floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel with a maxiumum working storage of 350,000 cubic metres.
Minimum cargo lifting size will be 150,000 barrels and the maximum will be 350,000 barrels, the spokesman said.
Petco is currently debating whether to sell the first cargo through a public tender.

The consortium developing the field is made up of Petronas Carigali, the exploration arm of Petronas, with 46.06 percent, PetroVietnam Exploration and Production with 12.5 percent, Canada's International Petroleum Corp with 26.44 percent and Sands Petroleum AB with 15 percent.
